rule: FR-4306 / FR-1201: every chapter has at least one widget question, or a gap a human has signed. A new kind is built only after Samuel approves it (decision 11, T356).

why: Three of the six anchor questions for this objective (ex6-1-1a, c, f) are rays, and ex6-1-1d, e and f have fraction or surd ends. number_line_marker's interval mode needs two whole-number ends inside +/-20, so the objective's most typical cases cannot be asked and the two templates cover only finite, whole-number intervals.

All six anchor questions read a graph. A question may not point at a [figure], and no existing kind draws a function for the student to read, so number_line_marker would reduce this to marking numbers the stem has already given. This lesson's graph has no misconception recorded for this objective, so even with this kind the diagnostics could not be filled until some are authored (for example: domain and range swapped, reading the plot window instead of the curve).

Evaluating $f(-1)$ is a typed number and no existing kind builds the substitution, so pair_plotter would only be an answer box with a grid. This objective has no misconception recorded in the graph either, so the kind would also need entries to be authored before its diagnostics could be filled.

pair_plotter takes a single point, so the table-to-points-to-line sequence the objective is about cannot be built. line_drawer in equation mode accepts any two points on the line, so it skips the table and never touches domain and range. number_line_marker's interval mode needs finite whole-number endpoints, so it cannot state an unrestricted domain or range. The objective also has no anchor question or listed misconceptions, so no template could be attached to it even if a kind fitted.

number_line_marker's interval mode needs both endpoints to be whole numbers inside a finite range, so the book's own answers (-infinity, infinity) and [-4, infinity) cannot be built, and a bounded stand-in would teach that the range stops somewhere. pair_plotter takes a single lattice point and shows no parabola, so asking for the turning point turns into typing (0, q) on a grid, an answer box in disguise. curve_sketcher grades a drawn stroke, not a domain, a range or an axis of symmetry. The listed misconceptions for this objective are all prerequisite ones (bracket notation, inequality signs), which the unbounded-interval instrument above would also be able to diagnose.

The one template written for this objective (mark both x-intercepts on a number line) holds only whole-number x-intercepts. number_line_marker cannot take an empty set, so 'recognise when there are no x-intercepts' is not expressible. It cannot take irrational values at 2 d.p., which are the book's actual answers (-0.63, 0.63 and so on). It carries no y-intercept at all. Those parts of the objective and the misconceptions that go with them (y-intercept-from-y-zero, no-root-taken, root-of-part) have no instrument.

curve_sketcher fits only part of this objective. It can show the sign of a (wrong-quadrants) and, with a catch-all off-target, the size of a, but it cannot construct the effect of q with a diagnosable misconception (vertically-displaced has no q error to map to on this objective's list, and a freehand stroke cannot say whether the student knows which way q moves the graph). The book's own questions are 'which graph matches this equation' and 'describe the transformation between two curves'; those need two live curves to compare, and a widget question may not point at a figure. This is a gap, not a forced fit.

The book's questions give a printed graph and a point and ask for a and q, and a widget question may not point at a [figure], so the graph itself must live inside the widget. No existing kind shows a given graph and lets the student set parameters against it. curve_sketcher could be given the asymptote and a point in the stem and asked for a sketch, but then the student can draw the curve through the point without ever calculating a or q, which is not the mathematics of this objective, and a point such as (-2, 5/2) is not on its whole-number snap. This objective also has no misconception ids recorded yet, so the three errors above would need to be added to the lesson's list before they can be mapped.

No existing kind builds this without becoming an answer box. pair_plotter could ask for the x-intercept, but the student only types a point, so it cannot refuse to plot the y-intercept and cannot express 'there is none', which is the key idea; its intercepts would also need whole numbers, whereas the book's are fractions (-3/2). number_line_marker could ask the student to mark the excluded x-value, but tapping 0 on a line is a recalled fact, not a construction. curve_sketcher would grade a stroke within one grid square, which cannot tell a y-intercept at (0, 2) from none, and it does not mark intercepts at all.

number_line_marker's interval mode needs a finite whole-number from and to inside a range of at most 24, so an unbounded range such as (-infinity, 3) cannot be specified, and parking the far end at the edge of the line would make the end handle a false answer. curve_sketcher is graded against one specific curve, not against a range, and a sketch of the curve does not make the student state the range. The lesson's list for this objective also holds no misconception of its own (only three inequality-direction ones from g10m4s7-1-1), so a new kind would need new misconceptions naming the range errors above.

pair_plotter would be an answer box in disguise: the student calculates the intercept on paper and then taps the lattice point that records her answer, and most exponential x-intercepts are not lattice points at all. curve_sketcher grades the whole curve, not an intercept, and no existing kind can represent 'there is no x-intercept' as a thing the student does.

The anchors (ex6-6-17, ex6-8-42, ex6-8-43) ask where a drawn graph is positive, increasing or decreasing. number_line_marker's interval mode cannot reach this: its range is whole numbers within ±20 and at most 24 wide, so θ from 0° to 360° does not fit except by an artificial unit of 30° that the student never sees in the book, and it shows no curve, so the student would be answering from recall or a typed rule, an answer box in disguise. curve_sketcher draws a curve, it does not read one. This objective also has no misconceptions on file, so diagnostics would have to be authored first.

The anchors ask the student to determine a and q FROM a drawn graph. curve_sketcher runs the other way (equation to curve), takes only whole-number a, and cannot carry the book's own values (a = 3/2 in ex6-6-1 and ex6-8-32). A sketch 'through two given features' with curve_sketcher is possible for whole-number cases such as ex6-6-2 (a = 4, q = -2), but that range reaches -6, past the instrument's -5..5 guidance, and the objective has no misconceptions on file, so no diagnostic could be authored. A parameter-fitting instrument is the construction the objective actually needs.

The only misconception this objective lists, negative-amplitude (reading the minus sign in y = -4 cos θ as part of the amplitude), has no predicate of its own on the cosine sketcher. Today the two templates have to map the residual off-target to it, which also fires for a sine-shaped or scribbled stroke. A dedicated predicate would make the diagnosis exact.

The objective asks for the sine and cosine graphs as horizontal shifts of each other. curve_sketcher fixes the period and has coefficients [a, q] only, with no phase parameter, so it cannot ask for or grade sin(θ + 90°). Its freehand sketch of cos θ rebuilds the previous objectives, not the shift relationship; the other kinds are not trigonometric at all. The anchors here are all 'read off the two graphs' with a [figure]. Note also that the lesson file lists no misconception for this objective, so the errors above would need to be seeded before a template could carry diagnostics.

The objective is to find a and q from two points, and the book's numbers include a = 1/2 (exercises 6-6-3 and 6-6-4) and q = −1 or −0.5. curve_sketcher's coefficients must be whole numbers and it scores a freehand stroke only 'within about one grid square', so it cannot tell a = 0.5 from a = 0 or 1 and cannot grade the book's own values. The question would also be an answer-box question in a sketch's clothing: the student would first calculate a and q, then draw. Seeding misconceptions for this objective (it has none listed) is also a precondition for any diagnostics.

The lesson file lists no anchor questions for this objective, so there is no parent_question_id to cite. Its only misconceptions are seven prerequisite ids about right-triangle ratios: choosing the hypotenuse, naming opposite and adjacent, sine written as opposite over adjacent. None of them is something a tangent sketch can reveal. Mapping asymptote-crossed or period-wrong onto one of them would show a student feedback about the wrong error. The diagnostics array must hold at least one honest entry, so no valid template exists.

The lesson file gives this objective an empty anchor_questions list and an empty misconceptions list. A template therefore has no parent_question_id to name and no own misconception id to put in diagnostics. FR-1215 refuses an id borrowed from another objective's list. Inventing an id or borrowing a parent from objective 6-3-4 would be forgery, so this is left for Samuel. Once the catalogue carries tangent-graph misconceptions and an anchor question, this objective should be the first to get a widget.

Every misconception listed for this objective is own=false and about right-triangle ratios: hypotenuse-not-longest-side, hypotenuse-not-opposite-right-angle, opposite-adjacent-fixed-by-position, ratio-at-the-right-angle, ratios-without-a-right-angle, reads-sides-from-other-angle and sine-as-opposite-over-adjacent. The nearest pairing, asymptote-crossed to sine-as-opposite-over-adjacent, would tell a student who drew one continuous wave that she mixed up sine's ratio. That is probably not her error: she more likely does not know that tangent breaks at 90°. Because of the one-predicate-one-misconception rule and the minimum of one diagnostic, no honest template can be written. A forced mapping would show a student wrong feedback.

The lesson file gives this objective an empty misconceptions list, so any diagnostics id would be refused (FR-1215). The 'a read as the y-value at 45° with q not subtracted' error is the dominant real error here, but the catalogue does not carry it. The template schema also requires at least one diagnostic. The anchors exist; the misconception ids do not.

The objective runs graph -> equation, and no existing kind does that. curve_sketcher runs the opposite way (equation -> freehand curve) and is scored within about one grid square, so it would accept a, q, or a-and-q off by one, which are exactly the near-miss equations this objective exists to separate; used with the points given in the stem it also tests the earlier 'sketch a parabola' skill, not the determination of a and q. line_drawer is linear only, and pair_plotter only places a point. A sketch-based fit would be a forced one. Note also that the lesson file lists only the four parabola misconceptions (g10m6s3-1-1) under this objective, although it covers hyperbola, exponential and trigonometric graphs; the hyperbola, exponential and trig families would need their own misconception ids added to this objective's list before a fitter could name their errors.

pair_plotter is the nearest kind but can only report swapped-coordinates, wrong-quadrant or off-target. All three of this objective's own misconceptions plot a point (0, k), so all of them land in off-target and cannot be told apart; mapping that one predicate would name the wrong error for two students in three. It also shows no function and no check, so plotting would be the answer typed on a grid, an answer box in disguise. curve_sketcher's exponential 'wrong-intercept' has the same flaw: the freehand tolerance of about one square cannot separate y = 2^x + 1 from y = 2^x + 2, and it does not name which wrong value was used. line_drawer handles one line at a time and cannot show an intersection of a line with a parabola or exponential. No existing kind fits without forcing it.

gaps.need_kind: number_line_marker (extension: an unbounded end, and non-whole ends)
gaps.description: Interval mode that accepts a ray: the student drags one end to the edge of the line and it becomes an arrow, with no circle, meaning the interval has no end there. The same mode would accept an end that is a fraction or a surd, such as $\frac{3}{4}$ or $-\sqrt{3}$, snapped to a labelled tick. The student marks $(-\infty, 7]$, $(35, \infty)$ or $(-\sqrt{3}, \infty)$ and sets the one finite end filled or hollow. It would diagnose a circle or square bracket put on an infinite end (a bracket on $\infty$ is never square), the finite end paired with the wrong inclusion, and the ray pointed the wrong way.
gaps.why: Three of the six anchor questions for this objective (ex6-1-1a, c, f) are rays, and ex6-1-1d, e and f have fraction or surd ends. number_line_marker's interval mode needs two whole-number ends inside +/-20, so the objective's most typical cases cannot be asked and the two templates cover only finite, whole-number intervals.

gaps.need_kind: graph_reader (new kind): the instrument draws the graph itself, the student bounds domain and range on the axes
gaps.description: The instrument draws the graph of a function in context, such as a straight segment from (0, 10) to (20, 0) for the rolling ball, or a segment ending in a filled point at (120, 100) for the car, on axes that run past the curve. The student drags a shaded span along the horizontal axis to set the domain and another along the vertical axis to set the range, and sets each end filled or hollow. A vertical guide the student drags along the horizontal axis reads off the function value live, which covers the 'after 6 s' style of question. The student constructs the two spans. Graded on the property: each span must run exactly over the curve's extent on its axis. It would diagnose domain and range swapped (the vertical extent given as the domain), the span taken as the whole visible window instead of the curve's extent, an end included or excluded wrongly, and a value read off the wrong axis.
gaps.why: All six anchor questions read a graph. A question may not point at a [figure], and no existing kind draws a function for the student to read, so number_line_marker would reduce this to marking numbers the stem has already given. This lesson's graph has no misconception recorded for this objective, so even with this kind the diagnostics could not be filled until some are authored (for example: domain and range swapped, reading the plot window instead of the curve).

gaps.need_kind: function_machine (new kind): an input dial into a named rule, with the output shown live
gaps.description: The student sees a function written in notation, such as $f(x)=x^{2}+1$, and an input dial. Dragging the dial shows the value substituted and the output. Tasks: set the input so that $f$ gives a target value ('find x with f(x) = 5': both -2 and 2 are accepted, graded on the property), and for compositions and sums, chain two machines so the output of one feeds the other. It would diagnose a negative input squared without brackets ($-1^2$ read as $-1$), $f(x+1)$ read as $f(x)+1$, the input put into the wrong place in the rule, and one of two inputs given when two exist.
gaps.why: Evaluating $f(-1)$ is a typed number and no existing kind builds the substitution, so pair_plotter would only be an answer box with a grid. This objective has no misconception recorded in the graph either, so the kind would also need entries to be authored before its diagnostics could be filled.

gaps.description: A grid with a table of values for a straight-line rule, for example $y = 2x - 1$ for $x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2$. The student places one point per x-value, tapping the grid above or below each column, then joins them. The widget would show whether the placed points are collinear and let the student join them into the line. A second step would ask for the domain and range, either as the set of all real numbers for the whole line, or as an interval when the stem restricts the x-values, for example $-2 \le x \le 3$ (the student marks the resulting y-interval). Diagnostics it could emit: swapped-coordinates on any point, a sign slip when evaluating the rule at a negative x (the point sits on the wrong side of the line), a missing point or an extra point, points that are not collinear, and, in the range step, the interval endpoints taken from the x-values rather than the y-values.
gaps.why: pair_plotter takes a single point, so the table-to-points-to-line sequence the objective is about cannot be built. line_drawer in equation mode accepts any two points on the line, so it skips the table and never touches domain and range. number_line_marker's interval mode needs finite whole-number endpoints, so it cannot state an unrestricted domain or range. The objective also has no anchor question or listed misconceptions, so no template could be attached to it even if a kind fitted.

gaps.description: A parabola y = ax^2 + q is drawn on a grid (the student does not draw it). Each axis carries a draggable shading handle pair. On the x-axis the student shades the stretch the curve lies over (the domain). On the y-axis she shades the stretch of values it reaches (the range). Each end can be set open, closed, or running off to infinity with an arrow. She also places the turning point and drags a line to the axis of symmetry, and marks the stretch of x where the curve is increasing. The widget would report: domain and range swapped; range given as [0, infinity) when q was ignored; range given as (-infinity, q] for an upward parabola, or [q, infinity) for a downward one (the sign of a); a closed end where the turning point is included and a hollow one where it is not; the axis of symmetry drawn as the x-axis or at x = q; increasing and decreasing swapped.
gaps.why: number_line_marker's interval mode needs both endpoints to be whole numbers inside a finite range, so the book's own answers (-infinity, infinity) and [-4, infinity) cannot be built, and a bounded stand-in would teach that the range stops somewhere. pair_plotter takes a single lattice point and shows no parabola, so asking for the turning point turns into typing (0, q) on a grid, an answer box in disguise. curve_sketcher grades a drawn stroke, not a domain, a range or an axis of symmetry. The listed misconceptions for this objective are all prerequisite ones (bracket notation, inequality signs), which the unbounded-interval instrument above would also be able to diagnose.

gaps.description: The plane for y = ax^2 + q is shown with its equation. The student drags one marker onto each point where the curve meets the y-axis and each point where it meets the x-axis, snapping to a 0.05 grid so a 2 d.p. answer such as (0.63, 0) is reachable. A 'no x-intercepts' switch is available for cases such as y = x^2 + 2. The curve is shown as the student places markers, so a marker that is off the curve is visibly off. It would report: only the positive x-intercept given; a y-intercept marked on the x-axis (y = 0 used for the y-intercept); x-intercepts claimed for a parabola that never reaches the axis (-q/a is negative); x-intercepts at plus or minus the quotient (the square root never taken); q taken as the gradient or the intercept swapped.
gaps.why: The one template written for this objective (mark both x-intercepts on a number line) holds only whole-number x-intercepts. number_line_marker cannot take an empty set, so 'recognise when there are no x-intercepts' is not expressible. It cannot take irrational values at 2 d.p., which are the book's actual answers (-0.63, 0.63 and so on). It carries no y-intercept at all. Those parts of the objective and the misconceptions that go with them (y-intercept-from-y-zero, no-root-taken, root-of-part) have no instrument.

gaps.description: A live hyperbola y = a/x + q drawn on a grid with its two dashed asymptotes, controlled by two steppers or sliders (a, whole numbers from about -6 to 6; q, whole numbers from -3 to 3). A fainter target graph is shown on the grid, or a second hyperbola, and the student sets a and q until the two coincide, or sets them to carry one given curve onto another ('what moves y = 2/x onto y = 2/x - 3?'). The student constructs the effect of each parameter by seeing it move: the sign of a flips the pair of quadrants, the size of a pushes the branches away from or toward the axes, q slides the whole graph and its horizontal asymptote up or down. It would diagnose the sign of a not deciding the quadrants (the right size with the wrong sign), a read backwards (the student first moves a down to push the curve away from the axes), and q mis-read as a sideways shift or with its sign flipped (the curve is the right shape at the mirror height).
gaps.why: curve_sketcher fits only part of this objective. It can show the sign of a (wrong-quadrants) and, with a catch-all off-target, the size of a, but it cannot construct the effect of q with a diagnosable misconception (vertically-displaced has no q error to map to on this objective's list, and a freehand stroke cannot say whether the student knows which way q moves the graph). The book's own questions are 'which graph matches this equation' and 'describe the transformation between two curves'; those need two live curves to compare, and a widget question may not point at a figure. This is a gap, not a forced fit.

gaps.description: A hyperbola y = a/x + q is drawn with a draggable marker constrained to the graph and a live readout of (x, y). The student drags the marker toward the y-axis and watches y run off the grid without the curve ever reaching x = 0; then drops a horizontal test line at different heights and counts how many times it meets the curve (once for most heights, never at y = q); finally lays a vertical test line along the y-axis to see that it meets the curve nowhere. The construction is the student's own marking of the excluded values on each axis (domain: every x except 0; range: every y except q) and, separately, of the x-intercept as the place where the horizontal test line at y = 0 meets the curve. It would diagnose assuming a y-intercept exists (the student insists on a point on the y-axis, or reports a value for it), the range given as y not equal to 0 instead of y not equal to q, and the x-intercept found by setting x = 0.
gaps.why: No existing kind builds this without becoming an answer box. pair_plotter could ask for the x-intercept, but the student only types a point, so it cannot refuse to plot the y-intercept and cannot express 'there is none', which is the key idea; its intercepts would also need whole numbers, whereas the book's are fractions (-3/2). number_line_marker could ask the student to mark the excluded x-value, but tapping 0 on a line is a recalled fact, not a construction. curve_sketcher would grade a stroke within one grid square, which cannot tell a y-intercept at (0, 2) from none, and it does not mark intercepts at all.

gaps.description: The same hyperbola_fitter instrument as the gap recorded for objective 1-2, but here the graph is part of the widget rather than a figure: the grid shows a target hyperbola drawn with its dashed horizontal asymptote and one labelled point A on it, plus a live curve y = a/x + q controlled by two steppers for a and q. The student reads q off the dashed asymptote, then finds a so that the live curve passes through A (the working 'a = (y - q) times x' can be shown beside the steppers as the student's own notes), until the live curve covers the target. The graph and the point are exactly what the book's questions show (for example point A at (-2, 5/2) with asymptote y = 2, or A at (-1, -5) with asymptote y = -3). It would diagnose q taken as the y-coordinate of A instead of the asymptote height, a taken as the x- or y-coordinate of A, and a with the wrong sign (the live curve lands in the wrong quadrants).
gaps.why: The book's questions give a printed graph and a point and ask for a and q, and a widget question may not point at a [figure], so the graph itself must live inside the widget. No existing kind shows a given graph and lets the student set parameters against it. curve_sketcher could be given the asymptote and a point in the stem and asked for a sketch, but then the student can draw the curve through the point without ever calculating a or q, which is not the mathematics of this objective, and a point such as (-2, 5/2) is not on its whole-number snap. This objective also has no misconception ids recorded yet, so the three errors above would need to be added to the lesson's list before they can be mapped.

gaps.need_kind: range_interval_marker (a number-line interval that supports an unbounded ray)
gaps.description: The student is given an exponential function in the form y = ab^x + q (for example y = -2^x + 3) and builds its range on a vertical number line: she drops one endpoint at a chosen height, sets it hollow or filled, and drags a ray from it toward +infinity or -infinity. A second, simpler control states the domain as all real numbers. The grader accepts exactly one ray: its endpoint at y = q, hollow (the curve never reaches the asymptote), pointing up when a > 0 and down when a < 0. It would name these errors: a filled endpoint (the asymptote counted as a value of y), the ray on the wrong side of q (the sign of a ignored), the endpoint put at the y-intercept instead of at q, and the domain and range exchanged (range answered as all reals, domain as y > q).
gaps.why: number_line_marker's interval mode needs a finite whole-number from and to inside a range of at most 24, so an unbounded range such as (-infinity, 3) cannot be specified, and parking the far end at the edge of the line would make the end handle a false answer. curve_sketcher is graded against one specific curve, not against a range, and a sketch of the curve does not make the student state the range. The lesson's list for this objective also holds no misconception of its own (only three inequality-direction ones from g10m4s7-1-1), so a new kind would need new misconceptions naming the range errors above.

gaps.need_kind: intercept_probe (drag a point along the curve and choose which variable to set to zero)
gaps.description: The curve y = ab^x + q is drawn from an equation in the stem (for example y = 2^x - 4, or y = 2^x + 3 for the no-intercept case). The student drags a probe point along the curve with a live (x, y) readout, and chooses which substitution to make from two toggles, 'let x = 0' and 'let y = 0', which show the equation with that value put in. To finish she must park the probe on the y-axis and on the x-axis and write down the readings; for a curve that never reaches y = 0 (a and q of the same sign) the probe closes in on the asymptote and the readout stays above 0, so the only correct finish is to declare 'no x-intercept'. It would diagnose: using y = 0 to find the y-intercept (the two rules swapped), claiming an x-intercept on the asymptote, reading the intercept off the number written in the equation, and swapping the coordinates of the point.
gaps.why: pair_plotter would be an answer box in disguise: the student calculates the intercept on paper and then taps the lattice point that records her answer, and most exponential x-intercepts are not lattice points at all. curve_sketcher grades the whole curve, not an intercept, and no existing kind can represent 'there is no x-intercept' as a thing the student does.

gaps.description: A sine graph y = a sin θ + q (the app draws it, so no [figure] is needed) sits over a labelled θ-axis from 0° to 360° with ticks every 30°. The student answers by CONSTRUCTING on that graph, not by typing: dragging the two ends of a highlighted stretch of the θ-axis (each end hollow or filled) to mark where the function is positive, negative, increasing or decreasing, and dragging a marker onto each turning point and each intercept. The stem names the property and the answer is graded as a set of intervals or points, so any construction with that property is accepted. Errors it would diagnose: marking the increasing/decreasing boundaries at the zeros (60° and 300°) instead of at the turning points (90° and 270°), which is confusing 'positive' with 'increasing'; giving 'decreasing' as the single interval 0° to 180° because the curve starts at the axis; the θ-coordinate of the maximum given as its height; and endpoints included where the function is strictly positive.
gaps.why: The anchors (ex6-6-17, ex6-8-42, ex6-8-43) ask where a drawn graph is positive, increasing or decreasing. number_line_marker's interval mode cannot reach this: its range is whole numbers within ±20 and at most 24 wide, so θ from 0° to 360° does not fit except by an artificial unit of 30° that the student never sees in the book, and it shows no curve, so the student would be answering from recall or a typed rule, an answer box in disguise. curve_sketcher draws a curve, it does not read one. This objective also has no misconceptions on file, so diagnostics would have to be authored first.

gaps.description: A target sine curve y = a sin θ + q is drawn on a θ-axis (0° to 360°, ticks every 30°) with two labelled points on it, as in ex6-6-1 and ex6-6-2, and the equation is hidden. The student drags two handles, one for a and one for q (each stepping in halves), and a live curve updates on top of the target until the two coincide. The grade is on the pair (a, q), so every route to it is accepted. Errors it would diagnose: reading a as the height of the peak instead of half the distance from trough to peak (a = 3 where the peak is 3 but the midline is 1.5); reading a as the full peak-to-peak distance; taking q from a turning point (the minimum or the maximum) instead of the midline; a and q exchanged; the sign of a lost for a graph that falls first.
gaps.why: The anchors ask the student to determine a and q FROM a drawn graph. curve_sketcher runs the other way (equation to curve), takes only whole-number a, and cannot carry the book's own values (a = 3/2 in ex6-6-1 and ex6-8-32). A sketch 'through two given features' with curve_sketcher is possible for whole-number cases such as ex6-6-2 (a = 4, q = -2), but that range reaches -6, past the instrument's -5..5 guidance, and the objective has no misconceptions on file, so no diagnostic could be authored. A parameter-fitting instrument is the construction the objective actually needs.

gaps.need_kind: curve_sketcher predicate for sine/cosine: reflected-in-x-axis (the sign of a), reporting an unreflected stroke when a < 0
gaps.description: Not a new kind but a missing predicate on curve_sketcher. For fn sine or cosine with a negative a, the scorer would report that the stroke has the right amplitude, midline and period but is the mirror image of the target (it starts at the maximum where the target starts at the minimum), analogous to opens-wrong-way for the quadratic and slope-sign-flipped for the line. The student would still sketch freehand exactly as in the two templates; what changes is that the refutation names the reflection, so 'the minus sign is a reflection in the x-axis, not part of the amplitude' fires on that cause and not on every unmatched stroke.
gaps.why: The only misconception this objective lists, negative-amplitude (reading the minus sign in y = -4 cos θ as part of the amplitude), has no predicate of its own on the cosine sketcher. Today the two templates have to map the residual off-target to it, which also fires for a sine-shaped or scribbled stroke. A dedicated predicate would make the diagnosis exact.

gaps.need_kind: phase_shifter: slide one trig graph horizontally onto another
gaps.description: The student sees y = sin θ and the target y = cos θ (or the reverse) on axes from 0° to 360°, and drags a handle that slides one curve left or right by a shift h, snapped to 15° steps, with the live rule updating, for example y = sin(θ + 30°). The task is stated by the property: 'slide the sine graph until it lies exactly on the cosine graph', and any h that is congruent mod 360° to the right shift is accepted (+90°, or −270°). A second prompt runs it the other way: 'cos θ = sin(θ + 90°); now slide cosine onto sine and write the shift'. The errors it would diagnose are: the shift in the wrong direction, which lands on sin(θ − 90°) = −cos θ (sign of the shift mis-read, as in (θ − a) read as θ + a); a shift of 180° (gives −sin θ, the 'upside down' graph); a half-way or 45° shift that matches neither; and sliding the wrong graph and reading the sign of the shift off the wrong curve.
gaps.why: The objective asks for the sine and cosine graphs as horizontal shifts of each other. curve_sketcher fixes the period and has coefficients [a, q] only, with no phase parameter, so it cannot ask for or grade sin(θ + 90°). Its freehand sketch of cos θ rebuilds the previous objectives, not the shift relationship; the other kinds are not trigonometric at all. The anchors here are all 'read off the two graphs' with a [figure]. Note also that the lesson file lists no misconception for this objective, so the errors above would need to be seeded before a template could carry diagnostics.

gaps.need_kind: cosine_fitter: set a and q so the live curve passes through two marked points
gaps.description: The widget shows two labelled points on the axes, such as A (180°; −1.5) and B (0°; −0.5), given by the stem's own numbers. The student sets a and q with two steppers (a in steps of 0.5, positive or negative; q in steps of 0.5) and the curve y = a cos θ + q redraws live. It is correct when the curve passes through both points, so any equivalent route (the y-intercept a + q and the range, or the turning points) is accepted. The errors it would diagnose are: taking the y-intercept as a (so ignoring q); reading the full height from minimum to maximum as the amplitude instead of half of it; the sign error from cos 180° = −1 (a read from the minimum with the wrong sign); and a and q swapped.
gaps.why: The objective is to find a and q from two points, and the book's numbers include a = 1/2 (exercises 6-6-3 and 6-6-4) and q = −1 or −0.5. curve_sketcher's coefficients must be whole numbers and it scores a freehand stroke only 'within about one grid square', so it cannot tell a = 0.5 from a = 0 or 1 and cannot grade the book's own values. The question would also be an answer-box question in a sketch's clothing: the student would first calculate a and q, then draw. Seeding misconceptions for this objective (it has none listed) is also a precondition for any diagnostics.

gaps.need_kind: No new kind. curve_sketcher (fn: tangent) fits; blocked by the data, not the instrument (no anchor question, no tangent-graph misconception)
gaps.description: The student would draw y = tan θ freehand over 0° to 360° (coefs [1, 0]), lifting the finger at θ = 90° and 270° and drawing each branch separately. That is the objective's own construction: join the plotted points with a smooth curve and mark where tan θ is undefined. The predicates that would matter are asymptote-crossed (drew straight through 90° or 270°), partial-coverage (stopped early or skipped a branch), period-wrong (drew one 360° wave instead of two 180° branches), fails-vertical-line-test and vertically-displaced. The calculator table-of-values step is arithmetic with a device. No existing kind builds it, and it should stay a worked step.
gaps.why: The lesson file lists no anchor questions for this objective, so there is no parent_question_id to cite. Its only misconceptions are seven prerequisite ids about right-triangle ratios: choosing the hypotenuse, naming opposite and adjacent, sine written as opposite over adjacent. None of them is something a tangent sketch can reveal. Mapping asymptote-crossed or period-wrong onto one of them would show a student feedback about the wrong error. The diagnostics array must hold at least one honest entry, so no valid template exists.

gaps.need_kind: No new kind. curve_sketcher (fn: tangent) fits exactly; blocked by the data (zero anchors, zero misconceptions on this objective)
gaps.description: This is the best fit in the lesson. The student sketches y = a tan θ + q freehand for 0° to 360° (for example coefs [2, 1], or [-1, -2]) and lifts the finger at each asymptote. The question isolates the two effects the objective names. q is a vertical shift, and a sets how steeply the branches rise. The widget can report vertical-shift-wrong (wrong midline, so q misapplied), amplitude-wrong (wrong steepness, so a misapplied), asymptote-crossed, period-wrong, partial-coverage, vertically-displaced and fails-vertical-line-test. Within the instrument limits, a is a nonzero whole number with |a| ≤ 3 and q is a whole number with |q| ≤ 3.
gaps.why: The lesson file gives this objective an empty anchor_questions list and an empty misconceptions list. A template therefore has no parent_question_id to name and no own misconception id to put in diagnostics. FR-1215 refuses an id borrowed from another objective's list. Inventing an id or borrowing a parent from objective 6-3-4 would be forgery, so this is left for Samuel. Once the catalogue carries tangent-graph misconceptions and an anchor question, this objective should be the first to get a widget.

gaps.need_kind: No new kind. curve_sketcher (fn: tangent) fits; blocked because the inherited misconceptions are all right-triangle ratio errors that no tangent-sketch predicate can reveal
gaps.description: The anchor (ex6-8-55a) asks for the domain of g(θ) = −tan θ. The student would sketch g over 0° to 360° (coefs [-1, 0]), lifting the finger at 90° and 270°. The domain exclusions, the asymptotes, the period of 180°, the intercepts at 0°, 180° and 360° and the unbounded range are then all constructed rather than recited. The widget's own refusal to let a stroke cross θ = 90° or 270° is the domain restriction made physical. The stem would say 'Sketch g(θ) = −tan θ for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°', never 'as in the diagram', because the anchor's [figure] must not be pointed at. Predicates that would be worth mapping are asymptote-crossed, period-wrong, partial-coverage, vertical-shift-wrong and amplitude-wrong.
gaps.why: Every misconception listed for this objective is own=false and about right-triangle ratios: hypotenuse-not-longest-side, hypotenuse-not-opposite-right-angle, opposite-adjacent-fixed-by-position, ratio-at-the-right-angle, ratios-without-a-right-angle, reads-sides-from-other-angle and sine-as-opposite-over-adjacent. The nearest pairing, asymptote-crossed to sine-as-opposite-over-adjacent, would tell a student who drew one continuous wave that she mixed up sine's ratio. That is probably not her error: she more likely does not know that tangent breaks at 90°. Because of the one-predicate-one-misconception rule and the minimum of one diagnostic, no honest template can be written. A forced mapping would show a student wrong feedback.

gaps.need_kind: curve_sketcher (fn: tangent), used in reverse, covers two of three anchors; a small parameter-fitting kind would cover all three. Both are blocked until this objective has misconceptions
gaps.description: Reverse construction: 'Draw the tangent curve y = a tan θ + q that passes through (0°, −3) and (45°, −2)', which is anchor ex6-8-34 with coefs [1, -3]. Anchor ex6-6-6 gives [1, 0]. The student has to read q from the y-intercept, because tan 0° = 0, and then get a as the rise from the intercept to the second point, a = y(45°) − q. Errors that would show are vertical-shift-wrong (q taken from the wrong point) and amplitude-wrong (a taken as the y-value at 45° without subtracting q, giving −2 where 1 is right). The third anchor, ex6-6-5 (q = 1/3, a = 3), cannot be expressed: curve_sketcher takes only whole-number q with |q| ≤ 3. Grading is also coarse, about one grid square, so a non-whole a would be hard to tell apart. A dedicated kind would give two drag handles: the y-axis handle sets q, and the second sets a. A live curve would be graded on passing through two labelled points, with rational a and q allowed. It would name 'a forgot to subtract q' as a specific miss.
gaps.why: The lesson file gives this objective an empty misconceptions list, so any diagnostics id would be refused (FR-1215). The 'a read as the y-value at 45° with q not subtracted' error is the dominant real error here, but the catalogue does not carry it. The template schema also requires at least one diagnostic. The anchors exist; the misconception ids do not.

gaps.description: The student would find the general-form equation that fits a graph. A grid shows a fixed target curve from one of the chapter's families (parabola y = ax^2 + q, hyperbola y = a/x + q, exponential y = a·b^x + q, sine or cosine y = a sin(theta) + q), with one or two lattice points on it labelled by the instrument itself, never by a stem figure. The general form is printed above the grid with a and q as stepper controls (b fixed for the exponential). A second curve is drawn live from the student's current a and q, and the answer is accepted when it coincides with the target, so any route to a and q is accepted and the property graded is 'passes through the marked points with the target's shape'. A 'substitute a marked point' readout shows both sides of the equation for the point the student picks, so the substitution step of the objective is something she does rather than recites. Errors it would diagnose: the sign of a wrong (the curve opens the other way, or lies in the other quadrants, or is reflected) -> mc:g10m6s3-1-1:sign-of-a-ignored; q left at 0 (turning point, asymptote or midline stays on the axis) -> mc:g10m6s3-1-1:q-ignored; q's sign flipped (shifted the wrong way) -> mc:g10m6s3-1-1:q-shift-wrong-direction; right orientation but wrong size of a (taking a bigger a as flatter) -> mc:g10m6s3-1-1:steepness-of-a-misjudged.
gaps.why: The objective runs graph -> equation, and no existing kind does that. curve_sketcher runs the opposite way (equation -> freehand curve) and is scored within about one grid square, so it would accept a, q, or a-and-q off by one, which are exactly the near-miss equations this objective exists to separate; used with the points given in the stem it also tests the earlier 'sketch a parabola' skill, not the determination of a and q. line_drawer is linear only, and pair_plotter only places a point. A sketch-based fit would be a forced one. Note also that the lesson file lists only the four parabola misconceptions (g10m6s3-1-1) under this objective, although it covers hyperbola, exponential and trigonometric graphs; the hyperbola, exponential and trig families would need their own misconception ids added to this objective's list before a fitter could name their errors.

gaps.description: The student would calculate an intercept or intersection by substitution and then place the result. The function (for example y = 2^x + 1, or a line and a parabola for intersections) is printed with NO curve drawn, so the answer cannot be read off a picture. The student chooses the substitution that gives the point asked for (x = 0 for the y-intercept, y = 0 for an x-intercept, equate the two expressions for an intersection) and plots the resulting point on a coordinate grid; a live check substitutes the plotted point into each function and shows which side fails to balance. In intersection mode the answer is a SET of points (graded as missed or extra points), so finding only one of two crossings is reported as that. The author names the likely wrong points, and the widget reports each one as its own predicate: for y = 2^x + 1, (0,3) -> mc:g10m6s7-1-2:power-at-zero-read-as-base (2^0 taken as 2), (0,1) -> mc:g10m6s7-1-2:power-vanishes-at-zero (2^0 taken as 0), (0,0) -> mc:g10m6s7-1-2:zero-reported-as-intercept (the 0 put in given as the 0 that comes out); for a line or parabola, the x-intercept plotted when the y-intercept was asked -> mc:g10m6s2-1-3:y-intercept-from-y-zero.
gaps.why: pair_plotter is the nearest kind but can only report swapped-coordinates, wrong-quadrant or off-target. All three of this objective's own misconceptions plot a point (0, k), so all of them land in off-target and cannot be told apart; mapping that one predicate would name the wrong error for two students in three. It also shows no function and no check, so plotting would be the answer typed on a grid, an answer box in disguise. curve_sketcher's exponential 'wrong-intercept' has the same flaw: the freehand tolerance of about one square cannot separate y = 2^x + 1 from y = 2^x + 2, and it does not name which wrong value was used. line_drawer handles one line at a time and cannot show an intersection of a line with a parabola or exponential. No existing kind fits without forcing it.
